meta_desc: Practise mean rates, tangents and Le Chatelier.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mean rate = change in mass or volume / time.

Units: g/s, cm^3/s, mol/s.

Draw a tangent at t = 20 s to find instantaneous rate.

If you change conditions, equilibrium shifts to oppose the change.

Increase pressure -> shifts to side with fewer gas molecules.

Increase temperature -> shifts in the endothermic direction.

N2 + 3H2 to 2NH3, exothermic.

High pressure (about 200 atm) favours fewer moles of gas (NH3).

Compromise temperature (about 450 C): lower would give more NH3 but too slow.

right (products)
no shift

no change

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
